territorial_scope.description: Applies to agencies, offices and authorities of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts and its political subdivisions as defined in the section.

evidence.quote: There shall be a commission within the executive office of technology services and security

summary.short: Bill H.64 would create a commission within the executive office of technology services and security to study Massachusetts government use of automated decision systems, survey those uses, and report annually with recommendations to the governor and legislature.
summary.long: Bill H.64 would insert a new Section 11 into Chapter 7D of the General Laws. It defines algorithm, artificial intelligence, automated decision system, Commonwealth or Massachusetts office, identified group characteristic, source code and training data. It creates a commission within the executive office of technology services and security to study and recommend regulations, limits, standards and safeguards for the use by the Commonwealth of automated decision systems that may affect human welfare. The commission's membership includes the secretary of technology services and security as chair, legislators, the attorney general, the state auditor, the inspector general, academic and advocacy representatives, and industry representatives. Members are to be appointed within 45 days of the effective date of the act. The commission must meet at least 10 times per calendar year, hold at least one public hearing, and broadcast its meetings over the internet. Its tasks include a survey of all Massachusetts office uses of automated decision systems, examination of transparency, auditability, data, intellectual property and due process issues, and a review of research on disparate outcomes. It must submit an annual report by December 31 that includes a public list of automated decision systems in use, policies and training, and contracts with third parties, together with recommendations such as areas where offices should not use such systems and procedures for explanations and for detecting disparate impacts. The bill sets no penalties and does not regulate private actors.

thresholds.note: The bill creates a study commission in the executive office of technology services and security. Its numbers are procedural deadlines (45 days for appointments, December 31 for the annual report), a meeting frequency (not fewer than 10 times per calendar year), and commission membership counts. None sets a scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit, or penalty cutoff, so none is coded as a threshold.
